newsitem.title: UK: Wool demand set for two percent rise in 1996-7.
newsitem.headline: Wool demand set for two percent rise in 1996-7.

text.p: World wool consumption is set to recover this year after plummeting by 40,000 tons in the 1995-6 season, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said in its quarterly commodity forecast.
Overall wool consumption will grow in the 1996-7 season, seeing even stronger growth in 1997-8 as stocks decline and prices rise, the report said.
The European Union is expected to drive the increase in demand up to 1.51 million tons clean in 1996-7 and spur a further 3.3 percent rise in 1997-8.
Millowners in Japan, where wool stocks are at historical lows, and clothing manufacturers in China are likely to buy an extra 6,000 and 4,000 tons respectively, the report said.

The EIU also forecast a price recovery for apparel wools which it said should reach 700 Australian cents per kg clean basis in 1998. Clean crossbred wools should be fetching 530 New Zealand cents per kg by the first half of 1998, it added.
